findings.label: flag_state_registry_legal_nationality_governance_layer
findings.memory: The legal-nationality/registry layer appears structurally distinct from classification, statutory survey and port-state control. It mediates vessel registration, flag-state jurisdiction and the institutional identity under which private or regional fleets operate; exact regimes and named registries require Evidence.

findings.label: outsourced_technical_commercial_ship_management_layer
findings.memory: Private fleets can separate beneficial ownership, registered ownership, technical management, commercial management and crewing/operations. Treating owner/operator as one actor can hide an outsourced management layer that is especially salient outside large public-company narratives.

findings.label: short_sea_river_sea_multipurpose_network_visibility
findings.memory: Deep-sea public-company salience may underweight short-sea, river-sea, multipurpose/general-cargo and archipelagic network structures. This looks more like a regional-network refinement than proof of a new universal semantic owner.

findings.label: inventory_bullwhip_double_ordering_destocking_judgment
findings.memory: A distinct shipper/retailer Judgment family concerns whether scarcity and long lead times caused safety-stock building, duplicate ordering or front-loading, and when the resulting inventory overhang would reverse into destocking. That is not identical to a generic goods-demand or congestion-normalization thesis.

findings.label: spot_contract_basis_and_rollover_lag_judgment
findings.memory: Participants could hold separate expectations for spot-rate normalization and lagged annual/longer-contract repricing. The persistence of contracted revenue or shipper cost after spot moves is a distinct timing/basis Judgment rather than merely another freight-rate forecast.

findings.label: service_reliability_capacity_guarantee_value_judgment
findings.memory: Shippers and forwarders could value guaranteed space/equipment or reliability differently from headline freight levels. Expectations about service restoration and willingness to pay for reliability form a useful refinement to the congestion/rate packet.

findings.label: goods_services_mix_and_sourcing_reconfiguration_judgment
findings.memory: A separate contemporaneous debate could concern whether elevated goods share, e-commerce, inventory policy and sourcing/nearshoring changes were temporary pandemic effects or durable trade-pattern shifts. Exact claims and chronology require Evidence.

findings.label: maritime_contracting_arbitration_general_average_salvage_risk_allocation_layer
findings.memory: Across tanker, bulk, liner and specialized shipping, standardized contracting, bills/charterparty allocation, arbitration/dispute resolution, general-average and salvage-type institutions form a risk-allocation layer that is not equivalent to insurance, regulation or operational service providers. Exact legal effects are Evidence-only.

findings.label: shipbroking_ffa_and_market_intermediation_price_discovery_layer
findings.memory: Physical chartering/S&P broking and freight-derivative or market-intermediation structures can connect freight expectations, asset values and hedging across subsectors. An index such as the Baltic Exchange is not the whole intermediary/price-discovery layer.

findings.label: port_agent_husbandry_local_service_bundle
findings.memory: The prior control review already assigns this local service bundle to P008/P137/P138; the challenger does not reopen it.

dedup_objections.why_distinct: Flag/legal nationality and registry identity govern a different institutional relationship from class rules, delegated statutory survey and port-state enforcement.
Outsourced technical/commercial management can be a separate control/operating layer even when ownership and crewing are already represented.
Private contract allocation and dispute-resolution institutions allocate commercial risk without being insurance coverage or public regulation.
Market intermediation/hedging/price discovery differs from an index publisher and from vessel debt/equity capital provision.
Inventory reversal and spot-versus-contract timing can produce different historical expectations and outcome clocks even when both relate to normalization.
